text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:

- SPD and Greens plan to request dismissal of Finance Minister Theo Waigel in parliament. Government coalition leaders plan to meet in Chancellery to discuss ways to plug budget gaps and gold revaluation plans.

- Germany energy rights reform plan remains controversial. Lobby groups welcome the planned reform, but there is resistance from local municipalities, unions and environmental groups against the government's plans.

- North Rhine-Westphalia deports more Bosnian refugees. A total of 53 Bosnian refugees have now been sent home against their will. A total of 9,000 Bosnians returned home voluntarily and about 66,000 Bosnians are still in the state.
- Bavarian CSU party remains united that euro should be as stable as the mark.

- Government tries to reach compromise with Bundesbank in dispute over gold revaluation. Chancellor Helmut Kohl says that only difference of opinion is on the timing of the revaluation. Finance Minister Theo Waigel plans to talk again with Bundesbank this week.

- Waigel in favour of higher taxes. Germany will probably slightly exceed the 60 percent debt level criteria for the Maastricht Treaty, says Hansgeorg Hauser, parliamentary state secretary for the finance ministry.

- Finance Minister Theo Waigel runs into opposition from his own Bavarian CSU party over his plans to revalue Bundesbank gold. Newspaper quotes sources in CSU saying Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber and CSU state parliamentary leader Alois Glueck had sharp criticism of Waigel for his plan.
- Opposition parties call for vote on dismissing Waigel.
- German cartel agency investigates Detusche Telekom for its cable TV network monopoly.
